missions.name: Public pixels: viz.render returns server-rendered SVG for all 13 types and dashboard HTML draws 11/11
missions.objective: Put the existing renderer on the public surface through one shared path. Measured today: viz.render returns a compiled Vega-Lite spec or a JSON-projected ECharts option and never bytes (zero svg/html/png occurrences in packages/mcp-server/src/tools/viz.render.ts; output controls are compact, echarts, includeNormalizedSpec, includeA11y at schemas/viz.render.input.json:315-340); dashboard.render output.html draws the 5 cartesian panels through renderVegaLiteToSvg (dashboard.render.html.ts:282-293) and sends the 6 ECharts-primary panel types (treemap, sunburst, sankey, force_graph, choropleth, bubble_map) to placeholderCell(..., 'geo') (:295-296, :383-399), a <section role=img> with a note and no image, as docs/api/dashboard-render.md:9 admits; @oods/viz-render already renders both engines deterministically (renderVegaLiteToSvg, renderEChartsToSvg + normalizeEChartsSvg) and artifact.certify uses both legs (artifact.certify.ts:486/529/905), but viz.render does not. Build: viz.render gains output.svg (boolean, default false), optional output.width and output.height, and returns svg, svgHash (sha256 hex of the returned bytes), svgBytes, svgRef (mirrors specRef for pipeline reuse) and a render echo {engine:'vega-lite'|'echarts', width, height, theme:'light', brand:'A'} (the theme/brand echo is fixed in m02 so m03 does not move the shape twice). The 5 cartesian types render through renderVegaLiteToSvg; the 8 ECharts-primary through renderEChartsToSvg with normalizeEChartsSvg applied before hashing, so svgHash is a normalized-structure hash for those 8 and a raw byte hash for the 5, documented as such. At default dimensions the cartesian render is intrinsic size exactly as artifact.certify's render leg (artifact.certify.ts:900-912 renders compiled at intrinsic size), so svgHash equals determinism.renderHash for the same normalized spec; caller width/height change the hash and the docs say so. A renderer failure returns a typed OODS-V1xx error with status error, never a silent spec-only success. compact is unchanged; svg is included only when requested. dashboard.render output.html draws the 6 ECharts-primary panels through the same ECharts leg at the panel's span dimensions (NOMINAL_DASHBOARD_WIDTH_PX / NOMINAL_ROW_HEIGHT_PX as the cartesian path already does); placeholderCell survives only for error panels; the docs sentence about placeholders is replaced. No new tool; registry and both bridge policy layers unchanged unless a schema change requires regeneration.
successCriteria: A 13-type render matrix spec calls the public viz.render handler with output.svg:true for every admitted chartType using the existing fixtures (the 5 cartesian and the 8 ECharts-primary golden inputs) and asserts a non-empty svg beginning with <svg, svgHash equal to sha256 of the returned bytes (normalized bytes for the 8), svgBytes equal to the byte length, and the render echo; every result is byte-identical across two consecutive calls (retained as a hash table)

For the 5 cartesian types, svgHash from viz.render at default dimensions equals determinism.renderHash from artifact.certify for the same normalized spec; a mutation bite that changes the compiled spec (or the shared renderer's output) moves both hashes together and the identity test detects a deliberate divergence

A renderer-throw bite (the VL or ECharts leg made to throw in-test) yields a typed OODS-V1xx error with status error and no svg field, never a spec-only status ok; the error code is registered in the error registry and docs

dashboard.render output.html for a fixture dashboard containing all 11 admitted panel types contains 11 rendered SVG chart cells and zero 'geo' placeholder sections; the placeholder remains only for an error panel fixture; outputHtmlHash is byte-stable across two calls; the existing cartesian panel bytes are unchanged (the dashboard HTML goldens that move are the 6 ECharts-primary cells and are updated with per-file attribution stating why)

Vega-Lite SVG output preserves role=graphics-object and aria-roledescription (the existing a11y-by-construction test extended to the public path); ECharts SVG output carries the normalized structural tokens per the s179 normalizer

Schemas, generated types (generate:schema-types --check), docs/api/viz-render.md and dashboard-render.md (docs:api --check), and the 14-file colocated golden list (ci-golden-list.guard) are updated and green; the viz-core, viz-render and mcp-server colocated viz suites pass; root typecheck passes; no full-suite capture

Build: (1) @oods/tokens exports cssVariablesByScope[brand][theme] (brand A|B, theme light|dark|hc, with the base scope folded in as the fallback layer) generated by the same Style Dictionary build that emits the six CSS scopes; the flat cssVariables export stays byte-identical (dist hash compared before and after) so vendored consumers (dashboard-demos at 852be47) and goldens are unaffected. missions.name: The chart in the generated application: VizAreaPreview becomes a real chart in HTML, React and Vue
missions.objective: Close the program's own park 'a preview frame is not a chart' for one object, one context and one chart type, through the public path. Measured today: VizAreaPreview is a placeholder div in all three renderers (React components-react/src/breadth.tsx:159-180, Vue components-vue/src/breadth.ts:158-179, HTML render/component-map.ts:1494-1511 'Area preview (640 x 360)'); it is declared only by traits/viz/mark-area.trait.ts:158-170 as a detail view extension (position top, priority 55); no compose template or design.compose.ts mentions it and no shipped object declares a viz/* trait, so it cannot reach a screen; the generated app and scripts/design-loop contain no chart runtime. Build: VizAreaPreview keeps its ID (nucleus catalog, COMPONENT_STYLE_IDS) and gains svg, title and description props: with svg it renders the server-rendered markup inline inside <figure role=img aria-label> (the renderer's own ARIA preserved, no script, no external references) in the HTML renderer, React and Vue with identical structure; without svg the placeholder stays. Subscription declares the existing viz/MarkArea trait; the view-extension collector places VizAreaPreview on Subscription/detail bound to a chart declaration {chartType:'area', x: payment date, y: amount in major units} over the object's payment events (the same events PaymentEventTimeline shows). code.generate resolves the declaration through the public viz.render SVG leg at generation time (theme and brand from compose preferences, default light/A) and embeds the SVG as a static per-file-hashed asset: the workflow app embeds one SVG per seeded record and selects by record id; single-screen detail artifacts expose svg as a typed prop and embed the seed-rendered SVG as the default. No client chart runtime is added; artifact contentHash and per-file hashes stay deterministic. Census movement is enumerated by class (h) chart placement and touches only objects that declare a viz trait.

missions.name: Certification takes the same scope, contrast per theme, and one executable visualization registry
missions.objective: Make certification and the record tell the same truth as the pixels. Measured today: artifact.certify input is spec plus optional data (schemas/artifact.certify.input.json), no theme or brand; its render leg is its own (renderHash = sha256(renderVegaLiteToSvg(compiled)) at intrinsic size, artifact.certify.ts:900-912) and contrast is render-measured for the 5 cartesian types on the light canvas only, with dark-theme contrast disclaimed as unverified at certify-contrast.ts:43/123/131 and artifact.certify.ts:180/400-416/952; coverage is 5 certified / 8 uncertified with accuracy rules V150-V153 (closed set) and V154-V159; no machine-readable registry of the 13 recipes exists (the admitted list is the viz.render input enum plus the ECharts-primary partition; certified-matrix.json pins 8 normalized hashes). Build: (1) artifact.certify accepts theme (light|dark|hc, default light) and brand (A|B, default A); its render leg renders at that scope through the shared renderer so determinism.renderHash equals viz.render's svgHash at default dimensions for every cartesian type and scope; contrast is measured on light and dark (and hc when m03 ships it) and the result rows per theme are retained in the output; the unverified-dark disclaimers are retired or made precise (say exactly which scope was measured). (3) scripts/product-reality/s190-viz-census.ts measures every cell by calling the public viz.render, dashboard.render, artifact.certify and design.compose handlers (no private imports) and writes the census JSON; a contract test asserts the registry equals the census output byte-for-byte after canonicalization.
